newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says stunned by Algeria massacre.
newsitem.headline: France says stunned by Algeria massacre.

text.p: France said on Wednesday it was stunned by Algeria's worst massacre in five years of slaughter and expressed solidarity with the people of its former north African colony.
Algerian authorities said Moslem rebels mercilessly hacked and shot 93 people to death in an orgy of savagery 25 km (15 miles) from Algiers that ended only as dawn approached on Tuesday.
"France learnt with horror the announcement of the massacre...which took 93 lives including women and children," French Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told reporters.

"France is worried and shocked by the blind and savage nature of the violence hitting Algeria. After these massacres, whose cruelty defies the imagination, France, which is stunned by the tragedy Algeria is living, expresses its emotion and solidarity with the Algerian people," Rummelhardt said.
Witnesses quoted by Algerian newspapers said between 40 and 50 men took part in the raid on an isolated farming community, Haouch Boughlef-Khemisti, in Bougara district.
The latest massacre, in which three children aged nine months to four years were killed, brought to nearly 300 those killed in the past few weeks in similar raids.

It coincided with the deadline for candidates to register for the first parliamentary elections since authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election in which Moslem fundamentalists had taken a commanding lead.
An estimated 60,000 people have died in the violence into which Algeria was plunged after the election was cancelled.
